newsitem.title: USA: Superior National to acquire Pac Rim.
newsitem.headline: Superior National to acquire Pac Rim.

text.p: Superior National Insurance Group Inc Tuesday said it signed a definitive agreement to acquire Pac Rim Holding Corp. for $54 million in cash.

Under terms of the deal, Superior National would pay approximately $3 to $3.10 per share to each of the common shareholders, debenture holders, assuming conversion of the debenture holders' interest, and warrant and option holders' interests, assuming exercise of the warrants and options.

Superior said the actual price is subject to a final analysis of Pacific Rim's loss reserves immediately prior to or at closing. The principal terms of the transaction were presented to the directors of each company over the weekend and were approved Tuesday.

Consummation of the transaction is subject to Superior National and Pacific Rim shareholder and regulatory approvals, and various other conditions, and is expected to occur early in 1997. The combination of the two companies will create California's largest independent workers' compensation specialist.

A group of investors including Insurance Partners, L.P., TJS Partners, L.P. and Superior National management will finance the transaction through the purchase of $18 million of newly issued Superior National common stock at $7.53 per share, which represents the average daily closing price of Superior National's common stock over an agreed-upon period of time preceding today's signing.

The remaining $36 million of the purchase price will be funded by a $44 million term loan provided by Chase Manhattan Bank, and $8 million of the loan proceeds will be used to redeem Superior National's outstanding long-term debt.

"Management believes the full integration of Pacific Rim has the potential to generate approximately $7.5 million of consolidated annual expense savings and that the acquisition should be immediately accretive to Superior National earnings," said J. Chris Seaman, executive vice president and chief financial officer. "This transaction will also enable the company to more effectively utilize its $80 million tax net operating loss carryforward, a valuable corporate asset.
